section: How does the current event compare with previous El Niños?
text:
How does the current event compare with previous El Niños?
The curves below track the same 34.8-pss fresh-pool boundary (S34.8), aligned on a common event-relative seasonal cycle to compare the timing, speed and maximum observed eastward extent of its displacement.



Fresh-pool boundary trajectories during the 2009–10, 2015–16 and 2023–24 El Niños and the ongoing 2026 event. The 2009–10 and 2026 trajectories are truncated where observations are unavailable or not yet available.

title: Dashboard: recent evolution
text:
MEI.v2
MEI.v2 is the dedicated NOAA PSL multivariate ENSO product combining oceanic and atmospheric information. It represents overlapping two-month seasons, identified by their ending month. The latest value is September 2026, corresponding to August–September 2026. The Pearson correlation with S34.8 is 0.850 (n = 200).



Comparison between the SSS-based indicator and NOAA PSL MEI.v2 (overlapping two-month seasons).

title: Dashboard: recent evolution
text:
HadISST Niño-3.4
This NOAA PSL HadISST Niño-3.4 index measures SST anomalies in the central-eastern equatorial Pacific relative to 1981–2010. The latest observation is July 2026. The Pearson correlation with S34.8 is 0.817 (n = 198).



Comparison between the SSS-based indicator and NOAA PSL HadISST Niño-3.4 SST anomalies (1981–2010).


Data availability note: the HadISST Niño-3.4 comparison ends in July 2026. MEI.v2 extends through September 2026 (the August–September season), and monthly relative Niño-3.4 extends through September 2026. Dates identify the first day of the represented month or MEI.v2 ending month.

C3S Niño-3.4
This comparison uses a Niño 3.4 SST index derived directly from the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) SST dataset, using a fixed 1991–2020 climatology to compute the anomaly.
The C3S-derived index provides a complementary SST-based reference for the SSS-based S34.8 indicator. This comparison uses twice-monthly sampling on the 1st and 15th and extends through September 2026. The latest September SST estimate is provisional. The Pearson correlation with S34.8 is 0.835 (n = 400).



Comparison between the SSS-based indicator and the C3S-derived Niño-3.4 SST index (1991–2020 climatology; twice-monthly sampling).

title: Dashboard: recent evolution
text:
Monthly relative Niño-3.4 (ERSSTv6, 1991–2020)
This NOAA CPC monthly relative Niño-3.4 product uses ERSSTv6 and a 1991–2020 reference period to account for the broader tropical warming background. These are individual monthly values, not a three-month running mean. The latest observation is September 2026. The Pearson correlation with S34.8 is 0.847 (n = 200).



Comparison between the SSS-based indicator and Monthly relative Niño-3.4 (ERSSTv6, 1991–2020).

title: Methods
text: This demonstrator follows the idea that the eastern edge of the western Pacific fresh pool can be tracked through a salinity isohaline near the equator. The 34.8-pss isohaline is used as a proxy for this boundary.

title: Methods
text:
Data source
The page is based on CCI+SSS satellite sea surface salinity fields, produced in the framework of ESA CCI+SSS and its transition toward ECMWF C3S.
For the Climate Data Record period, the demonstrator uses the soon-to-be-released CCI+SSS version 6 product, covering 2010–2024. An interim Climate Data Record updated in near-real time is currently in development and is expected to become operational at the end of 2026.
In the meantime, the near-real-time extension currently used for the latest months is based on the CATDS SMOS+SMAP product, which is also updated in near-real time.

title: Methods
text:
Index definition
The experimental SSS-based index is based on the longitudinal position of the 34.8-pss isohaline in the equatorial Pacific.
Configuration used here:
Isohaline: 34.8 pss
Latitude band: 2°S–2°N
Longitude range: 128°E–270°E
Temporal resolution: monthly
Reference period: 2010–2024
Product version: CCI+SSS v6.3 for the CDR period, with CATDS SMOS+SMAP for the current near-real-time extension

title: Methods
text:
Comparison indices
The SSS-based index is compared with NOAA PSL MEI.v2, NOAA PSL HadISST Niño-3.4, a C3S-derived Niño 3.4 index, and Monthly relative Niño-3.4 (ERSSTv6, 1991–2020) from NOAA CPC. Additional reference indicators may be considered as the analysis develops.
MEI.v2 represents overlapping two-month seasons, identified by their ending month, with a 1980–2018 reference period. The latest value is September 2026 (August–September 2026). HadISST Niño-3.4 uses monthly SST anomalies relative to 1981–2010 and extends through July 2026. Monthly relative Niño-3.4 uses ERSSTv6 with a 1991–2020 reference period and extends through September 2026; these are individual monthly values, not a three-month running mean.
The NOAA comparisons use the exact timestamp intersection with first-of-month S34.8 positions, starting on 1 February 2010. No interpolation, date shifting, or additional smoothing is applied. The matched comparisons end in September 2026 for MEI.v2 and monthly relative Niño-3.4 (200 samples each), and July 2026 for HadISST Niño-3.4 (198 samples). Their Pearson correlations with S34.8 are 0.850, 0.847, and 0.817, respectively.
The C3S Niño 3.4 index is derived from SST anomalies in the Niño 3.4 region in the C3S combined sea surface and sea ice surface temperature dataset, using a fixed 1991–2020 climatology. The C3S comparison uses twice-monthly sampling on the 1st and 15th and extends through September 2026 (Pearson correlation 0.835; n = 400). The latest September SST estimate is provisional.
